hero.lead: International Economics & Trade student. Former class leader. Sports team leader. Boxer. The one you hand the plan to when the activity actually has to happen.

about.lead: Most candidates will tell you what they would do. I'd rather show you what I have already done — as a class leader, as a sports team leader, and as the person teachers handed the mic to when it was time to organize something real.
about.sub: This page is not a promise. It is an evidence file: the roles I have carried, the sport that built my discipline, the events I helped organize, and the way I work with people. Read it, then decide.

experience.title: Class Leadership
experience.description: I served as the person responsible for my class — the link between students, teachers and administration. I passed information both ways, raised problems until they were solved, and kept class affairs moving. It taught me that a leader is measured by what stops being other people's problem.

experience.title: Sports Team Leadership
experience.description: I led a sports team through actual competitions. Training schedules, match arrangements, keeping eleven different temperaments pointed at one goal. Under pressure you learn fast: clear roles, honest communication, and nobody left guessing.

experience.title: School Event & Activity Organization
experience.description: I helped teachers organize school parties, events and activities — the practical side: planning, logistics, dividing tasks, and being the person who checks the details twice. This is the closest thing to a trial run for the role I'm asking for.

experience.title: Private English Tutor
experience.description: I tutored English one-to-one. Teaching forces a skill most people skip: reading the other person in real time and adjusting. Explaining something until it lands is communication at its most honest level — and it's the same skill that keeps a team briefed and calm.

experience.title: Family Business — Games Trade
experience.description: I worked in my family's business buying and selling games. Purchasing, pricing, negotiating, dealing with all kinds of customers. When you've handled real transactions, organizing a budget for an activity is not theory — it's a smaller version of what you already do.

experience.title: Independent Travel
experience.description: I have traveled independently from a young age. Routes, bookings, budgets, plans that break and get rebuilt on the move. Travel is self-management under real conditions — and it is where I learned to stay calm and solve problems when the plan stops working.

why.title: Communication
why.text: I've spent years moving information between people — as a class leader between students and teachers, as a tutor between confusion and clarity, in business between buyer and seller. Ideas only work when they actually arrive.

why.title: Organization
why.text: Parties, events, school activities — I've been on the organizing side with our teachers, not just in the crowd. Timelines, logistics, checklists, and the unglamorous work that makes an event look effortless.

why.title: Teamwork
why.text: Basketball, volleyball, football — years of team sports taught me to coordinate with people, trust roles, and chase one objective together. Teams beat collections of individuals. I know the difference from the inside.

why.title: Leadership
why.text: I've carried real responsibility twice: as the responsible person for my class, and as the leader of a competing sports team. Leadership isn't a title I'm asking for — it's a habit I already have.

why.title: Delegation
why.text: A strong team is not one person doing everything — it's the right person in the right role. I've led enough teams to know how to spot what each person is genuinely good at, and assign accordingly.

why.title: Problem Solving
why.text: Activities rarely go exactly to plan — venues fall through, people arrive late, weather changes its mind. Boxing and independent travel both trained the same reflex: stay calm, adapt, fix it.

why.title: Energy
why.text: Gym, basketball, volleyball, football, running — an active life isn't a hobby, it's the fuel for an active student environment. I naturally bring pace and momentum to everything I organize.

why.title: Responsibility
why.text: When I accept responsibility, I take it seriously — as a class leader, as a team captain, as the person trusted with real tasks in a family business. People hand me things because I bring them back done.

quote.text: Leadership is not doing everything yourself. It's knowing who can do what — and bringing those strengths together.

activities.lead: I want our activities to be organized, enjoyable, inclusive — and worth giving up an evening for. No unrealistic promises. Just real, doable ideas run properly:
activities.strip: Inclusive by default · Small enough to actually happen · Organized enough to be worth it

pillars.title: Organized
pillars.text: Clear plans, clear roles, start and end on time. An activity without structure is just a gathering.

pillars.title: Enjoyable
pillars.text: Designed around what students actually want — not what looks good on a report.

pillars.title: Inclusive
pillars.text: Different energy levels, different interests, different comfort zones. Everyone gets a way in.

pillars.title: Actually happening
pillars.text: Realistic scale, honest logistics, follow-through. Small and real beats big and fake.

list: Friendly sports competitions — football, basketball, volleyball
Cultural exchange evenings — food, music, stories
Student interaction events that mix people up
Recurring mini-challenges worth showing up for

sports.story1: Boxing took me to regional, national and continental competitions. Two things happen when you compete at that level: you learn that preparation beats talent, and you learn that nobody is coming to do the work for you. Both lessons transferred directly to organizing real activities.
sports.story2: Around the ring, I live in team sports — basketball, volleyball, football — plus the gym and running. Team sports teach you to coordinate and trust; the gym teaches you to show up when nobody is watching. That mix is exactly what running practical activities demands.

hero.lead: 国际经济与贸易专业学生。曾任班级负责人。运动队队长。拳击手。当一项活动必须真正办成时，大家会把方案交给的那个人。

about.lead: 大多数候选人会告诉你他们将做什么。我更愿意展示我已经做过的事——作为班级负责人、作为运动队队长、作为老师们在组织活动时放心托付的那个人。
about.sub: 这个页面不是承诺，而是一份证据档案：我承担过的角色、塑造我纪律性的运动、我协助组织的活动，以及我与他人共事的方式。看完，再做判断。

experience.title: 班级负责人
experience.description: 我曾担任班级负责人——同学、老师与学院之间的桥梁。我双向传递信息，跟进问题直到解决，让班级事务持续运转。这让我明白：一个负责人，是用“别人不再需要操心的事”来衡量的。

experience.title: 运动队队长
experience.description: 我带领一支运动队参加正式比赛：训练安排、赛事协调，让十几个性格不同的人指向同一个目标。压力之下你学得很快：分工清晰、沟通坦诚、不让任何人掉队。

experience.title: 校园活动组织
experience.description: 我协助老师组织校园晚会、活动和比赛——负责实操层面：规划、后勤、分工，以及把细节检查两遍的那个人。这是对我竞选岗位最接近真实的一次演练。

experience.title: 英语家教
experience.description: 我做过一对一英语家教。教学逼你掌握一项多数人会忽略的能力：实时读懂对方并随时调整。把一件事讲到对方真正听懂，是最诚实的沟通——也是让团队始终信息同步、心态稳定的同一种能力。

experience.title: 家族生意——游戏买卖
experience.description: 我在家族的游戏买卖生意里工作：采购、定价、谈判，与形形色色的顾客打交道。真正经手过交易之后，为一场活动做预算就不再是理论——它只是你每天都在做的事的缩小版。

experience.title: 独立旅行
experience.description: 我很早就开始独立旅行：路线、订票、预算，以及计划被打断后在路上重建计划。旅行是真实条件下的自我管理——正是在那里，我学会了在计划失效时保持冷静、动手解决。

why.title: 沟通
why.text: 多年来我一直在人与人之间传递信息——作为班级负责人在同学与老师之间，作为家教在困惑与理解之间，在生意里在买方与卖方之间。想法只有真正送达才有价值。

why.title: 组织
why.text: 晚会、活动、比赛——我一直在老师身边负责组织执行，而不只是人群中的一个。时间表、后勤、清单，以及让一场活动看起来毫不费力的那些幕后工作。

why.title: 团队协作
why.text: 篮球、排球、足球——多年的团队运动教会我与人协调、信任分工、朝同一个目标冲刺。团队胜过一群个人。这种区别，我在场上体会过。

why.title: 领导力
why.text: 我两次承担过真实的责任：作为班级负责人，作为参赛运动队的队长。领导力不是我此刻请求的头衔——它已经是我一直保持的习惯。

why.title: 知人善任
why.text: 强大的团队不是一个人包揽一切——而是把合适的人放在合适的位置。带过队伍之后我明白：先看清每个人真正擅长什么，再去分配。

why.title: 解决问题
why.text: 活动很少完全按计划进行——场地有变、人员迟到、天气翻脸。拳击和独立旅行训练出同一种反射：冷静、调整、解决。

why.title: 活力
why.text: 健身、篮球、排球、足球、跑步——运动不只是爱好，它是活跃的校园氛围的燃料。我组织的每一件事，都自带节奏和推进力。

why.title: 责任心
why.text: 凡是我接下的责任，我都会认真扛住——作为班级负责人、作为队长、作为在家族生意里被托付实事的那个人。别人放心把事情交给我，因为我总会办完交回来。

quote.text: 领导力不是事事亲力亲为，而是清楚谁擅长什么——并把这些长处聚到一起。

activities.lead: 我希望我们的活动被组织好、真正有趣、人人可参与——并且值得你为它留出一个晚上。不开空头支票，只做真实可行的事：
activities.strip: 默认包容 · 规模务实 · 组织到位

pillars.title: 有组织
pillars.text: 计划清晰、分工明确、准时开始按时结束。没有结构的活动只是一次聚集。

pillars.title: 有意思
pillars.text: 围绕同学们真正想玩什么来设计——而不是看起来好看就行。

pillars.title: 够包容
pillars.text: 不同的精力水平、不同的兴趣、不同的舒适区。每个人都能找到入口。

pillars.title: 真办成
pillars.text: 务实的规模、诚实的后勤、可靠的执行。小而真实，胜过大而空洞。

sports.story1: 拳击把我带到了区域赛和全国赛的赛场。在那个 level 上你会学到两件事：准备胜过天赋；没有人会替你完成备战。这两课，我直接用在了组织真实活动上。
sports.story2: 拳台之外，我活跃在篮球、排球、足球这些团队运动里，加上健身和跑步。团队运动教会我协调与信任；健身教会我没人监督时也要出现。这个组合，正是运营实践活动所需要的。
